subject: Financial Accounting
examFormat: Two papers taken at one sitting. Paper 1 has fifty multiple-choice questions, all to be answered in 1 hour for 25 marks. Paper 2 (2 1/2 hours) has Section A, four essay questions on Theory of Financial Accounting (answer two, 15 marks each), and Section B, five essay questions on Financial Accounting Practice (answer three, 15 marks each).
excluded: 11.8 Statement of Cash Flow, topic 12 (Accounting for Value Added Tax) and topic 15 (Information Technology in Accounting) because they are marked as available to candidates in Ghana only.

topics.name: Introduction to Financial Accounting
objectives: Describe the history, nature and functions of accounting
Identify the users of accounting information
State the stages in the accounting process
State the characteristics of accounting information

topics.name: The Accounting Equation and Double Entry Principles
objectives: Explain the accounting equation
State the purpose and functions of source documents
Explain subsidiary books
Classify accounts in the ledger
Prepare the analytical cash book, including the petty cash book
Prepare a trial balance
Prepare bank reconciliation statements
Correct errors and prepare a Suspense Account

topics.name: Accounting Concepts
objectives: Explain the meaning of accounting concepts
Identify the types of accounting concepts
State the significance of accounting concepts
State the limitations of accounting concepts

topics.name: The Final Accounts of a Sole Trader/Proprietorship
objectives: Prepare trading, profit and loss accounts/income statement
Prepare the balance sheet/statement of financial position
Make adjustments to final accounts

topics.name: Provisions and Reserves
objectives: Account for provision for doubtful debts/allowance for doubtful debts
Account for provision for discounts
Explain depreciation: concepts, reasons for recording and methods (straight line, reducing balance, sum of the years digits, revaluation)
Account for depreciation
Distinguish revenue and capital reserves

topics.name: Manufacturing Accounts
objectives: State the purpose of Manufacturing Accounts
Classify costs in Manufacturing Accounts
Prepare the final accounts of a manufacturing concern

topics.name: Control Accounts and Self-balancing Ledgers
objectives: Explain the meaning and uses of control accounts
Identify the types: sales ledger control and purchases ledger control
Prepare control accounts
Reconcile control accounts

topics.name: Single Entry and Incomplete Records
objectives: Explain the meaning and limitations of single entry and incomplete records
Compute profit or loss from opening and closing balance sheets
Convert single entry to double entry
Prepare final accounts from a set of incomplete records
Compute mark up and margin

topics.name: Accounts of Not-for-Profit Making Organizations
objectives: Explain the meaning and terminologies of not-for-profit making organizations
Prepare receipts and payments accounts
Prepare the subscriptions account
Prepare income and expenditure accounts
Compute the accumulated fund
Prepare the balance sheet
Compute profit or loss from income generating activities

topics.name: Partnership Accounts
objectives: Explain the nature and formation of partnership
Explain partnership agreements/deed
Prepare profit and loss appropriation accounts
Prepare partners' capital accounts and balance sheet
Account for the admission of a new partner
Treat goodwill and revaluation of assets
Account for the dissolution of partnership
topics.content: Questions will not be set on Garner v. Murray and piecemeal realization.

topics.name: Company Accounts
objectives: Explain the nature and formation of a company
Identify the types of companies and shares
Account for the issue of shares
Explain loan capital, debentures/loan notes and mortgages
Prepare the final accounts of a company for internal use only
Interpret accounts using simple ratios
Prepare the purchase of business account
topics.content: Separate questions may be set to meet statutory requirements of individual countries; candidates' answers must meet the statutory requirements of individual countries.

topics.name: Departmental and Branch Accounts
objectives: Explain the meaning and importance of departmental and branch accounts
State the differences between a department and a branch
Prepare departmental accounts
Prepare Branch Accounts excluding foreign branches
Account for inter-branch transactions

topics.name: Public Sector Accounting
objectives: Explain the meaning of public sector accounts and distinguish them from private sector accounts
Identify the sources of public revenue
Distinguish capital from recurrent expenditures
Prepare simple government accounts

topics.name: Miscellaneous Accounts
objectives: Explain the meaning, introduction and terminologies of, and prepare simple Joint Venture Accounts
Explain the meaning, introduction and terminologies of, and prepare simple Consignment Accounts
Explain the meaning, introduction and terminologies of, and prepare simple Contract Accounts
Explain the meaning, introduction and terminologies of, and prepare simple Hire Purchase Accounts

topics.name: Financial System
objectives: Explain the meaning and components of the financial system
Explain the meaning, functions and features of the money market, the capital market and the insurance market
Describe the methods of raising funds from the capital market: offer for sale, offer for subscription, rights issue and private placement
State the requirements for accessing the capital market
State the benefits of the capital market to investors, government, the economy and individual companies
Identify the types and features of, and reasons for, regulation
